title: Sampling for RNA, Protein, and Nutrients from Phage Infection Experiments
author: Sarah Giuliani
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.f27bqhn

steps.title: Collect Samples
steps.instruction: Collect 10ml from each experimental bottle/tube into a 15ml conical tube using a serological pipet.

steps.title: Centrifuge Samples
steps.instruction: Spin tubes for 15 minutes at 4700 rpm (4816 x g) in a swinging bucket rotor.

steps.title: Process Supernatants
steps.instruction: Handle the supernatants based on whether the cell-free fraction is required for analyzing dissolved inorganic/organic nutrients or phage particles.

substeps.instruction: To collect cell-free fraction: decant supernatants into labeled sterile 50 ml conical tubes, pooling the RNA and protein supernatants to create a 20ml combined supernatant
To discard cell-free fraction: decant supernatant into a waste container

steps.title: Freeze and Store Pellets
steps.instruction: Flash-freeze cell pellets in 15 ml tubes using liquid nitrogen and store in a -80°C freezer until analysis.

steps.title: Filter Supernatant
steps.instruction: Filter the 20ml combined supernatant using a syringe and filter setup.

substeps.instruction: Remove the plunger from a 20ml clean syringe
Attach a new 0.2µm syringe filter to the syringe
Pour the 20ml combined supernatant into the syringe barrel
Replace the plunger and filter the supernatant into appropriate tubes (e.g., one 15ml conical tube and one 5ml snap-cap Eppendorf tube)

steps.title: Process Replicates
steps.instruction: Repeat the filtration process for each sample, reusing the same syringe for replicates of the same condition/treatment.

steps.title: Store Filtered Samples
steps.instruction: Store the 0.2µm filtered samples at the appropriate temperature based on the target analyte.

substeps.instruction: Store at 4ºC if analyzing phage particles in the filtrate
